verses.text: When Yahweh your God brings you into the land where you go to possess it, and casts out many nations before you, the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, seven nations greater and mightier than you;
and when Yahweh your God delivers them up before you, and you strike them; then you shall utterly destroy them. You shall make no covenant with them, nor show mercy to them;
neither shall you make marriages with them. You shall not give your daughter to his son, nor shall you take his daughter for your son.
For he will turn away your son from following me, that they may serve other gods. So Yahweh’s anger would be kindled against you, and he would destroy you quickly.
But you shall deal with them like this. You shall break down their altars, dash their pillars in pieces, and cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their engraved images with fire.
For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God. Yahweh your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth.
Yahweh didn’t set his love on you, nor choose you, because you were more in number than any people; for you were the fewest of all peoples:

but because Yahweh loves you, and because he desires to keep the oath which he swore to your fathers, Yahweh has brought you out with a mighty hand, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
Know therefore that Yahweh your God himself is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness with them who love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations,
and repays those who hate him to their face, to destroy them. He will not be slack to him who hates him. He will repay him to his face.
You shall therefore keep the commandments, the statutes, and the ordinances, which I command you today, to do them.
It shall happen, because you listen to these ordinances, and keep and do them, that Yahweh your God will keep with you the covenant and the loving kindness which he swore to your fathers.

He will love you, bless you, multiply you. He will also bless the fruit of your body and the fruit of your ground, your grain and your new wine and your oil, the increase of your livestock and the young of your flock, in the land which he swore to your fathers to give you.
You shall be blessed above all peoples. There shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your livestock.
Yahweh will take away from you all sickness; and none of the evil diseases of Egypt, which you know, will he put on you, but will lay them on all those who hate you.
You shall consume all the peoples whom Yahweh your God shall deliver to you. Your eye shall not pity them: neither shall you serve their gods; for that would be a snare to you.
If you shall say in your heart, “These nations are more than I; how can I dispossess them?”
you shall not be afraid of them. You shall remember well what Yahweh your God did to Pharaoh, and to all Egypt;

the great trials which your eyes saw, the signs, the wonders, the mighty hand, and the outstretched arm, by which Yahweh your God brought you out. So shall Yahweh your God do to all the peoples of whom you are afraid.
Moreover Yahweh your God will send the hornet among them, until those who are left, and hide themselves, perish from before you.
You shall not be scared of them; for Yahweh your God is among you, a great and awesome God.
Yahweh your God will cast out those nations before you little by little. You may not consume them at once, lest the animals of the field increase on you.
But Yahweh your God will deliver them up before you, and will confuse them with a great confusion, until they are destroyed.
He will deliver their kings into your hand, and you shall make their name perish from under the sky. No one will be able to stand before you, until you have destroyed them.

You shall burn the engraved images of their gods with fire. You shall not covet the silver or the gold that is on them, nor take it for yourself, lest you be snared in it; for it is an abomination to Yahweh your God.
You shall not bring an abomination into your house, and become a devoted thing like it. You shall utterly detest it, and you shall utterly abhor it; for it is a devoted thing.

footnotes.content: God names the nations—Hittites, Girgashites, and the rest—as if He knows His people will ask, 'Who are these?' Already the promise is three times answered: *He* brings you in, *He* casts them out, and they are fewer than they seem. Fear meets its answer before fear can settle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The command reads harsh until you see what it guards: a people preserved. No covenant with them, no mercy that compromises—not cruelty, but the hard love of a father who sees what a friendship with folly costs. This is the boundary that keeps the next generation free.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The command about marriage cuts deepest because love pulls hardest. Your daughter, his son—the bond is real and tender. Yet Moses speaks plainly: the heart that is divided learns to serve a divided god. The forbidding is a fence around love itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here is the reason, and it is not hidden: a household divided in worship divides the next generation's heart. He will turn away your son—not by force, but by the slow weight of a parent's allegiance. I've watched this across generations. The Lord sees it coming and speaks with urgency because He loves the children you cannot yet see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Break the altars, dash the pillars, burn the idols—not in vengeance, but in surgery. These are not abstract commands; they are the removal of what calls the eye and ear away from the true God. Sometimes devotion to the Lord requires us to actively dismantle what once held us captive.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You are holy—not because you earned it, but because God chose it and you. Holiness begins as a gift, received before it becomes a practice. The Lord has already set the mark upon you. Now you must live as what you already are.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You were the fewest of all peoples—the smallest of all crowds. Here the Lord gently overturns what humans count as reason. He chose not the mighty or the numerous, but the small, so that when blessing comes, no one can say the people made themselves great.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Because Yahweh loves you—there it is, the heart of it. Not because you deserved choosing, but because love itself moves without keeping score. The redeemed ones are redeemed, not by their worth, but by His. And that is the only foundation that holds when everything else shakes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Faithful God—God who keeps His word through a thousand generations. One lifetime is such a small thing set against such a promise. In our impatience, we forget: the Lord thinks in centuries and counts the grandchildren we will never see. His word spans the gap that our doubt cannot cross.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He repays those who hate Him—not with the slowness of human justice, but face to face, with no delay. The command is not meant to comfort us, but to sober us. There is no distance so great that the Lord's judgment cannot find us, and no secret so hidden that it remains hidden from Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Keep the commandments—today. Not tomorrow, not when you feel ready, but this day. The Lord calls obedience not as a distant goal, but as the path underfoot right now. To do them is not to earn favor you haven't already received, but to live as if you believe the love that chose you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If you listen and keep and do them—the condition is not hidden or harsh, but plain as a threshold. Step over it, and you step into the keeping of the covenant. The Lord does not hide the path; He stands at the door and shows it clearly to those who will see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He will love you, bless you, multiply you—grain and wine and oil, livestock and young. The Lord speaks to people rooted in earth and season, promise in the language of harvest and flock. Blessing is not abstract but concrete: hands that work, ground that yields, mouths that are fed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No barrenness among you—children and increase in all things. For a people who knew the sting of Egyptian bondage, this is the deepest comfort: the Lord will give you a future, a name, a line unbroken. Not every age hears this as its own promise, yet every age needs the comfort that the Lord does not forget to bless.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All sickness taken away—the diseases you have seen in Egypt will not touch you. The Lord speaks not only of safety from enemies, but of healing and wholeness. Yet we know that sickness comes to the faithful too; here Moses speaks to the reign of the Lord, who is God over all things, even the evil we fear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Consume all the peoples whom Yahweh delivers—your eye shall not pity them. This command meets the hardest part of the human heart: mercy. Yet pity for the enemy who draws your children away is not mercy but a trap. The Lord knows: compassion for what enslaves us is not compassion but betrayal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: These nations are more than I; how can I dispossess them?—Here is the doubt that comes in the quiet moment, when you count the spears of the enemy and see only your own smallness. The question is honest; the Lord does not despise it, only what comes after it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You shall not be afraid of them. You shall remember well what Yahweh did—fear is answered not by argument, but by memory. The Lord does not say, 'Your fear is baseless,' but, 'Remember.' Remember what you have seen, what He did to Pharaoh, how the sea opened. Memory of mercy is the antidote to fear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The great trials which your eyes saw, the signs and wonders—Moses anchors the promise in what they have witnessed: the darkness, the water, the escape. These are not myths but lived memory. So shall Yahweh do to all the peoples whom you fear. He appeals to what they know, not to blind faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh will send the hornet among them—a small thing, yet enough to scatter the strong. The Lord does not always work through the sword; sometimes through the unseen, the humbling, the turning to flight before human strength. His victory comes by ways we would never choose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You shall not be scared of them; for Yahweh your God is among you, a great and awesome God. The cure for fear is not confidence in your own strength, but the knowledge that the One greater than all is standing beside you. Fear that holds His presence in mind finds little room to grow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He will cast out those nations little by little—not all at once, lest the beasts of the field multiply and overwhelm you. Here is the Lord's patience shown as kindness: He knows that a people cannot bear everything at once, and that gradual victory teaches what sudden conquest cannot.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He will deliver them up and confuse them with a great confusion—the enemy falls not always by the sword, but by confusion and loss of counsel. I have seen this in the unraveling of what seemed strong: the enemy begins to scatter against himself, and victory comes through no plan we made.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their kings into your hand, and you shall make their name perish—the memory of the enemy is erased from the earth. Yet even in victory, remember: it is the Lord's hand that brings the king low, not your hand alone. The glory that remains is His alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Burn their engraved images, but do not covet the silver or gold—here is a hard lesson: in victory, do not take what glitters. The ornament of the false god carries its own curse. The spoil that looks precious is often the snare that catches the victor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Do not bring an abomination into your house—readers today hear an echo in this: what we invite into our homes shapes the hearts within them. The warning is not about objects alone, but about the small permissions we grant, the compromises we justify. The Lord is saying: guard the threshold of your house as you would guard your heart, for what enters will take root.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
